summary:
SSS (Smart Safety System) is an autonomous, zero-waste, closed-loop fire suppression and toxic gas management system engineered for closed space habitats such as the International Space Station (ISS) and future Mars colonies. In microgravity, the absence of natural convection causes smoke and deadly Carbon Monoxide (CO) to scatter unpredictably across the cabin, while shipping heavy pre-filled extinguisher cylinders from Earth and venting contaminated cabin air waste millions of dollars in payload mass and vital life-support resources. SSS solves this challenge using an active forced-suction system paired with a lightweight two-stage chemical filter (Activated Carbon and Hopcalite catalyst) that converts toxic CO into an oxygen-depleted (<16% O2), CO2-and-nitrogen-rich extinguishing mixture stored onboard for free, precision-targeted fire suppression. Integrated with an HC-05 Bluetooth module and a custom real-time Web Mission Control dashboard, SSS protects crew lives, reduces main ECLSS reactor strain, and scales seamlessly to terrestrial factories, tunnels, and smart homes.

details:
SSS operates as an intelligent closed-loop life-support pre-processor aligned with NASA's Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) and In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) principles. Because hot gases and smoke do not rise naturally in microgravity, SSS utilizes high-torque fans and diaphragm pumps to generate active forced airflow that captures scattered smoke and toxic gas mixtures. Stage 1 uses high-density activated carbon to trap thick smoke, soot, and toxic organic vapors, protecting sensitive station hardware from clogging. Stage 2 utilizes a Hopcalite catalyst to oxidize deadly Carbon Monoxide into Carbon Dioxide (2CO + O2 -> 2CO2) at ambient temperature, eliminating heavy gas-separation machinery for fire suppression.
Chemical consumption of O2 inside the filter combined with automated suction cut-off preserves an oxygen-depleted (<16% O2), CO2-and-nitrogen-rich gas mixture inside an isolated emergency tank. Upon flame detection, dual IR flame sensors guide a 180-degree servo aiming nozzle directly toward the fire source using pulse-pumping, conserving stored gas by 40% while extinguishing flames without contaminating cabin air. Excess CO2 integrates seamlessly with Sabatier and Oxygen Generation Systems to recycle clean water and breathable oxygen.
The system features four intelligent operating modes and multi-pattern crew alerts: SAFE MODE (energy-saving circulation with green LCD telemetry), WARNING MODE (high-power forced suction stores CO2 in the tank with slow intermittent seat vibration alerts), DANGER GHAZAL (audio-visual alarms, rapid intense seat haptic vibration, and full gas purging), and CRITICAL FIRE (180-degree servo locks onto flame coordinates and extinguishes the fire automatically). Power circuits are isolated across dual breadboards to eliminate electromagnetic interference, and a perforated decompression chamber protects pumps from over-pressure. An HC-05 Bluetooth module streams live sensor telemetry to our custom HTML5/JavaScript Web Mission Control App, featuring a live CO ppm waveform chart, a 180-degree thermal flame radar map, hardware status indicators, and manual override buttons.
Tools & Hardware Used: Arduino Uno microcontroller, MQ-7 Carbon Monoxide sensor, Dual IR Flame sensors, 180° Micro Servo motor, 3 DC Diaphragm Pumps, High-Torque Suction Fan, HC-05 Bluetooth Module, Vibration Haptic Motors, I2C 16x2 LCD Display, Buzzer, Dual Breadboards, C++ (Arduino IDE with Watchdog Timer protection), HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript.
Future Scope & Earth Impact: Future upgrades include Peltier thermoelectric modules (TEC1-12706) to harvest exothermic filter reaction heat into clean electricity instead of wasting energy on cooling radiators, central control circuit integration for automated airtight cabin doors and crew notifications, 3D digital thermal flame arrays, and an autonomous oxygen-delivery rescue rover. On Earth, SSS provides an affordable, scalable safety solution for factories, tunnels, and smart homes under the "Ana W Abny Green Community Initiative."
